items: Logging: The process of tracking and recording activities, events, or errors in an application, useful for debugging, error tracking, and understanding system behavior.
Logback: A logging framework that is the default choice for Spring Boot applications for logging.

SLF4J (Simple Logging Facade for Java): A simple facade or abstraction for various logging frameworks (e.g., java.util.logging, log4j). SLF4J provides a common interface for different logging frameworks to be used in the application.
Problem Diagnosis: Helps quickly identify issues in the system during execution.
Debugging: Provides valuable insights into the flow of the application, enabling developers to trace errors.
Maintenance: Ensures that developers or system administrators can monitor the system after deployment.

content.text: As developers, you may want to control what gets logged and how it is formatted. Spring Boot provides several ways to customize logging behavior:

items: Spring Boot uses SLF4J (Simple Logging Facade for Java) as a standard API to log messages.
By default, Spring Boot configures Logback for logging.
logger.error(): Logs an error message along with an exception.
Use AOP to separate logging concerns from business logic.
This ensures that logging is handled in a modular way, making your code cleaner.
@AfterThrowing: AOP annotation to log exceptions after they are thrown by methods in the repository or service layers.

content.text: Spring Boot uses Logback by default to log messages. The output includes:

items: Date and Time: When the log message is generated.
Log Level: INFO, ERROR, DEBUG, etc.
Thread Name: The thread where the log message was generated.
Logger Name: Name of the logger generating the log message.
Log Message: The actual message.
Logging to a File: By default, Spring Boot logs to the console. To log to a file, configure the application.properties file.

content.code:
logging.file=application.log          # Log to a specific file
logging.path=/var/logs                # Log to a specific directory

content.text: Custom Log Patterns: Customize the log pattern by using a logback-spring.xml configuration file.

items: This configuration changes the log format to only show the date, time, and message.

content.text: Logging Levels: You can specify the logging level for different packages or classes.

content.code: logging.level.com.infosys=DEBUG  # Set logging level to DEBUG for a specific package

content.text: While Logback is the default logging framework, you can switch to Log4j2 by excluding Logback and adding Log4j2 dependencies.
